blurb: Landmarks, old country names and the languages of the world

questions.q: The Inca citadel of Machu Picchu sits high in the Andes of which country?
questions.fact: American explorer Hiram Bingham brought Machu Picchu to world attention in 1911.

questions.q: The ancient city of Petra, seen in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade, is in which country?
questions.fact: The Nabataeans carved Petra's famous Treasury facade into a sandstone cliff about 2,000 years ago.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Khazneh (1989 film; Nabataean; early 1st century AD)

questions.q: Tom Cruise climbed the outside of which skyscraper in Mission: Impossible - Ghost Protocol?
questions.fact: The Dubai tower was called Burj Dubai until it opened in January 2010, when it was renamed.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa (renamed at 4 Jan 2010 opening); khaleejtimes.com (Cruise stunt, 2011 film)

questions.q: Which king built Neuschwanstein, the castle that inspired Disneyland's Sleeping Beauty Castle?
questions.fact: Construction of Neuschwanstein began in 1869, atop the ruins of older castles.
questions.src: Verified: nationalgeographic.com Neuschwanstein article (Ludwig II; begun 1869 on castle ruins; inspired Disneyland castle)

questions.q: Which country changed its name from Siam in 1939?
questions.fact: It briefly went back to Siam in 1945, but the name Thailand became permanent in 1949.
questions.src: Verified: ebsco.com research starter 'Siam Changes Its Name to Thailand' (5 Jun 1939; back to Siam 1945; permanent 1949)

questions.q: Which island nation was called Ceylon until 1972?
questions.fact: The tea industry kept the old name, so Sri Lankan tea is marketed as Ceylon tea.

questions.q: Which country was called Zaire from 1971 to 1997?
questions.fact: Muhammad Ali and George Foreman's 1974 Rumble in the Jungle was fought in Kinshasa, Zaire.
questions.src: Verified: worldatlas.com 'which country was formerly called Zaire' (1971-1997); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rumble_in_the_Jungle

questions.q: Which country officially renamed itself Eswatini in 2018?
questions.fact: The change was announced during celebrations of 50 years of independence; eSwatini means place of the Swazi.
questions.src: Verified: aljazeera.com 2018/04 'Swaziland king changes country's name to Kingdom of Eswatini' (19 Apr 2018, during 50-years-of-independence celebrations; 'place of the Swazi')

questions.q: What is the official language of Brazil?
questions.fact: Brazil is home to more Portuguese speakers than any other country, Portugal included.

questions.q: In The Lion King, the name Simba is the word for lion in which language?
questions.fact: In Swahili, Rafiki means friend and hakuna matata means no worries.
questions.src: Verified: jenmansafaris.com 'real meanings of Lion King names'

questions.q: Black Panther used which real South African language as the official language of Wakanda?
questions.fact: Actor John Kani, who played King T'Chaka, pushed for Xhosa and was one of the film's language consultants.
questions.src: Verified: okayafrica.com 'How isiXhosa became the official language of Wakanda' (Kani proposed it on Civil War set; one of the main language consultants)

questions.q: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and which other?
questions.fact: Romansh, a descendant of Latin, is spoken mainly in the southeastern canton of Graubunden.

blurb: Capital cities, shared borders and which country sits where

questions.q: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.fact: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857, over Toronto, Montreal, Kingston and Quebec City.
questions.src: Verified: historicalsocietyottawa.ca 'Queen Victoria chooses Ottawa' (letter 31 Dec 1857; rival cities)

questions.q: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.fact: Canberra was built as a planned capital, a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.q: Casablanca is Morocco's largest city, but which city is its capital?
questions.fact: The classic 1942 film Casablanca was shot in California, not Morocco.

questions.q: Which city is the southernmost capital of an independent country?
questions.fact: New Zealand moved its capital from Auckland to Wellington in 1865.
questions.src: Textbook (Wellington ~41.3 S; others ~34-35 S). Verified: nzhistory.govt.nz 'Parliament sits for the first time in Wellington' (capital moved from Auckland, 1865)

questions.q: Which tiny country on the Mediterranean coast is bordered on land only by France?
questions.fact: Monaco is the world's second-smallest country by area; the first Monaco Grand Prix was held in 1929.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco_Grand_Prix (first race 14 Apr 1929; not held 1938-47, 1949, 1951, 1953-54, 2020). Area: textbook (Vatican smaller)

questions.q: Besides Belize, which country borders Mexico to the south?
questions.fact: Guatemala is home to Tikal, one of the largest cities of the ancient Maya.

questions.q: Victoria Falls lies on the border between Zambia and which country?
questions.fact: Its local name, Mosi-oa-Tunya, means the smoke that thunders.

questions.q: Which country borders every other South American country except Chile and Ecuador?
questions.fact: Brazil also borders France, through the overseas region of French Guiana.
questions.src: Textbook (Brazil borders 9 of the other 11 SA states plus French Guiana)

questions.q: Which European country is famously shaped like a boot?
questions.fact: Italy completely surrounds two independent countries: San Marino and Vatican City.

questions.q: Game of Thrones filmed King's Landing in Dubrovnik, a walled city in which country?
questions.fact: Visitors can walk the medieval stone walls that encircle Dubrovnik's entire old town.

questions.q: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.fact: Lesotho's lowest point is about 1,400 meters up, the highest low point of any country.

questions.q: The fabled desert city of Timbuktu is in which African country?
questions.fact: Timbuktu sits near the Niger River on the southern edge of the Sahara.

blurb: Volcanoes, earthquakes, geysers and the rocks beneath our feet

questions.q: Old Faithful geyser is in which national park?
questions.fact: Yellowstone, established in 1872, is widely considered the world's first national park.

questions.q: Johnny Cash's 1963 hit shares its name with which zone of volcanoes around the Pacific?
questions.fact: Most of the world's earthquakes and active volcanoes occur along the Ring of Fire.

questions.q: In 2010, ash from Eyjafjallajokull grounded flights across Europe. Which country is it in?
questions.fact: The name roughly means island mountain glacier in Icelandic.

questions.q: Which volcano was born in a Mexican farmer's cornfield in 1943?
questions.fact: Paricutin kept erupting for nine years before finally going quiet in 1952.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paricutin (began 20 Feb 1943 in Dionisio Pulido's cornfield; eruptions ended 1952)

questions.q: Which scale, devised in 1935, became the best-known way to rate earthquake strength?
questions.fact: Each whole-number step up the Richter scale means seismic waves about 10 times larger.
questions.src: Textbook (Charles Richter, 1935; Mercalli dates from 1902; USGS: each whole number = tenfold increase in measured amplitude)

questions.q: What is the point on Earth's surface directly above an earthquake's origin called?
questions.fact: The underground spot where a quake actually starts is called the hypocenter, or focus.

questions.q: Which supercontinent's name comes from the Greek for all the Earth?
questions.fact: German scientist Alfred Wegener argued in the early 1900s that the continents had drifted apart.
questions.src: Textbook (pan = all, Gaia = Earth; Gondwana from an Indian region, Laurasia = Laurentia+Eurasia, Rodinia from Russian)

questions.q: California's San Andreas Fault marks where the Pacific Plate meets which other plate?
questions.fact: Along the fault, the two plates grind sideways past each other rather than colliding head-on.

questions.q: On the Mohs hardness scale, which mineral ranks at the top with a 10?
questions.fact: German mineralogist Friedrich Mohs created the scale in 1812; soft talc sits at the bottom with a 1.

questions.q: Which light, bubbly volcanic rock is famous for floating on water?
questions.fact: Pumice stones are tumbled with denim to give jeans their stonewashed look.

questions.q: Which volcanic glass, used to build Nether portals in Minecraft, forms when lava cools very fast?
questions.fact: Ancient peoples, including the Aztecs, used obsidian for knives, arrowheads and mirrors.
questions.src: Textbook (geology); Minecraft Nether portal frame is obsidian

questions.q: Marble forms when heat and pressure transform which rock?
questions.fact: That makes marble a metamorphic rock, from the Greek for change of form.

blurb: Flags described in words, national animals and famous emblems

questions.q: Which country's flag has a red maple leaf on a white square between two red bands?
questions.fact: Canada's maple leaf flag was first raised in 1965.

questions.q: Which country's flag shows a blue starry globe inside a yellow diamond on a green field?
questions.fact: The banner across the globe reads Ordem e Progresso, Portuguese for order and progress.

questions.q: On Mexico's flag, an eagle eating a snake is perched on what?
questions.fact: It recalls the Aztec legend of the sign that showed where to found Tenochtitlan, now Mexico City.
questions.src: Textbook (eagle on a prickly pear cactus)

questions.q: Which country has a national flag shaped like two stacked triangles?
questions.fact: It is the only national flag that is not a rectangle or square; it is crimson with a blue border.

questions.q: New Zealanders are often nicknamed after which flightless bird?
questions.fact: Kiwi are about the size of a chicken and come out mostly at night.

questions.q: What mythical creature is the national animal of Scotland?
questions.fact: A unicorn and a lion hold up the shield on the royal coat of arms of the United Kingdom.

questions.q: The peacock is the national bird of which country?
questions.fact: India's national animal is the Bengal tiger.

questions.q: Which antelope is South Africa's national animal and the nickname of its rugby team?
questions.fact: Springboks are known for pronking: bouncing high into the air on stiff legs.

questions.q: Since 1782, which bird has been the emblem on the Great Seal of the United States?
questions.fact: Benjamin Franklin once wrote to his daughter that the turkey was a more respectable bird.

questions.q: Which two animals hold up the shield on Australia's coat of arms?
questions.fact: Sprays of golden wattle, Australia's national flower, frame the shield.

questions.q: The Red Cross emblem is a color-reversed version of which country's flag?
questions.fact: The Red Cross movement was founded in Geneva, Switzerland, in 1863.

questions.q: Which flower is the emblem of Japan's imperial family?
questions.fact: Japan's monarchy is often called the Chrysanthemum Throne.

blurb: Famous routes, airports and bucket-list landmarks

questions.q: Which famous US highway ran from Chicago to Los Angeles?
questions.fact: Route 66 opened in 1926, and Pixar's 2006 film Cars is set in a town along it.

questions.q: The Appalachian Trail runs from Georgia to which state?
questions.fact: Its northern end is Mount Katahdin, the highest peak in Maine.

questions.q: The famous Orient Express train made its first run in 1883 from which city?
questions.fact: Its eastern goal was Constantinople, today's Istanbul; Belgian Georges Nagelmackers created it.
questions.src: Verified: smithsonianmag.com 'True history of the Orient Express' (left Paris 4 Oct 1883 for Constantinople; Belgian Georges Nagelmackers)

questions.q: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from Moscow to which Pacific port city?
questions.fact: Along the way, the line crosses the Ural Mountains, from Europe into Asia.

questions.q: LAX is the airport code for which city?
questions.fact: The X has no meaning; it was added when airport codes grew from two letters to three.
questions.src: Verified: knaviation.net and airwaysmag.com history of LAX (old code LA; X is a filler with no meaning)

questions.q: Which supersonic airliner flew passengers across the Atlantic from 1976 to 2003?
questions.fact: Concorde could fly from London to New York in about three and a half hours.
questions.src: Verified: historyhit.com Concorde facts (service 1976-2003; London/Paris-New York about 3.5 hours)

questions.q: Changi Airport, home to an indoor waterfall called the Rain Vortex, serves which country?
questions.fact: The waterfall sits inside Jewel Changi, a garden-filled complex that opened in 2019.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewel_Changi_Airport (Rain Vortex inside Jewel; opened 17 Apr 2019, official opening Oct 2019)

questions.q: Chicago O'Hare's airport code, ORD, comes from its original name. What was it?
questions.fact: The airport was later renamed for Navy pilot Edward Butch O'Hare.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O'Hare_International_Airport (originally Orchard Field; renamed 1949 for Navy ace Edward 'Butch' O'Hare)

questions.q: Which city's opera house is famous for its roof of white, sail-like shells?
questions.fact: Danish architect Jorn Utzon quit the project in 1966 and never saw the finished building in person.
questions.src: Verified: smithsonianmag.com and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorn_Utzon (resigned 1966; opened 1973; never saw it)

questions.q: When it was built in 1923, what did the Hollywood sign originally say?
questions.fact: It began as an ad for a housing development; the last four letters came down in 1949.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Sign (1923 HOLLYWOODLAND housing ad; LAND removed 1949)

questions.q: In the Harry Potter films, the Hogwarts Express crosses which real Scottish railway landmark?
questions.fact: The curving concrete viaduct carries Scotland's West Highland Line near Loch Shiel.

questions.q: Which is the oldest of the bridges that span Venice's Grand Canal?
questions.fact: The stone Rialto Bridge was completed in 1591, replacing earlier wooden bridges.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rialto_Bridge (stone bridge 1588-1591; oldest of four Grand Canal bridges; replaced wooden bridges)

blurb: Mountains, rivers, lakes and deserts around the globe

questions.q: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
questions.fact: Everest is named for George Everest, a British surveyor general of India in the 1800s.

questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak, is in which country?
questions.fact: Kilimanjaro is a dormant volcano standing only about 3 degrees south of the equator.

questions.q: In the 2018 film Free Solo, Alex Honnold climbs which Yosemite wall without ropes?
questions.fact: Free Solo won the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature.

questions.q: Because Earth bulges at the equator, which peak's summit is farthest from Earth's center?
questions.fact: Ecuador's Chimborazo summit sits about 2 kilometers farther from Earth's center than Everest's.
questions.src: Verified: guinnessworldrecords.com 'Farthest mountain peak from Earth's centre' (Chimborazo ~6,384 km; more than 2 km farther than Everest)

questions.q: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
questions.fact: In places, the Grand Canyon is more than a mile deep.

questions.q: Which river flows through the heart of Paris?
questions.fact: Despite a name meaning new bridge, the Pont Neuf is the oldest standing bridge across the Seine in Paris.
questions.src: Verified: structurae.net Pont Neuf (oldest standing bridge across the Seine in Paris; completed 1606-07)

questions.q: Which river flows through Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade?
questions.fact: It inspired The Blue Danube, the famous 1867 waltz by Johann Strauss II.

questions.q: Which wide estuary lies between Buenos Aires and Montevideo?
questions.fact: Its name means river of silver, and Argentina's name also comes from argentum, Latin for silver.

questions.q: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.fact: Counting cold deserts too, Antarctica is the largest desert on Earth.

questions.q: Which of the Great Lakes lies entirely within the United States?
questions.fact: Lakes Michigan and Huron meet at the Straits of Mackinac and share the same water level.

questions.q: Luke Skywalker's desert home, Tatooine, was mostly filmed in which country for 1977's Star Wars?
questions.fact: The planet's name comes from Tataouine, a real town in southern Tunisia.

questions.q: Which is the world's deepest lake, plunging more than a mile down?
questions.fact: Siberia's Lake Baikal holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.
questions.src: Textbook (max depth ~1,642 m; ~20% of surface fresh water)

blurb: Clouds, storms and the science behind the forecast

questions.q: Which puffy, cotton-ball clouds usually mean fair weather?
questions.fact: Cumulus comes from the Latin word for heap or pile.

questions.q: Towering thunderstorm clouds with flat, anvil-shaped tops are called what?
questions.fact: Big ones can tower more than 10 kilometers high, taller than Mount Everest.
questions.src: Textbook (Cb tops commonly 12-18 km; Everest 8.85 km)

questions.q: Fog is essentially which type of cloud resting at ground level?
questions.fact: Fog forms when air near the ground reaches its dew point, usually by cooling but sometimes by gaining moisture.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fog (fog 'usually resembling stratus'; forms by cooling or by added moisture/evaporation)

questions.q: Which English amateur scientist gave clouds names like cumulus and cirrus in the early 1800s?
questions.fact: Howard, a London chemist, first presented his Latin cloud names in a lecture in 1802.
questions.src: Verified: lindahall.org Scientist of the Day 'Luke Howard' (English chemist; Askesian Society, Dec 1802)

questions.q: What is the calm center of a hurricane called?
questions.fact: The strongest winds swirl in the eyewall, the ring of storms surrounding the eye.

questions.q: What are hurricanes called when they form in the Pacific near Japan and the Philippines?
questions.fact: Hurricane, typhoon and cyclone are all regional names for the same kind of storm.

questions.q: To guess how many miles away lightning struck, count seconds until thunder, then divide by what?
questions.fact: Thunder is the boom of air expanding explosively after lightning heats it in an instant.

questions.q: In 1971, which scientist introduced a scale rating tornadoes by the damage they cause?
questions.fact: An updated version, the Enhanced Fujita or EF scale, took over in the US in 2007.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_Fujita_scale (Fujita scale introduced 1971; EF in US use from 1 Feb 2007)

questions.q: Which instrument measures air pressure?
questions.fact: Italian scientist Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer around 1643.

questions.q: By tradition, if Punxsutawney Phil sees his shadow, how many more weeks of winter are left?
questions.fact: The first official Groundhog Day at Gobbler's Knob, Pennsylvania, was held in 1887.
questions.src: Verified: history.com Groundhog Day history (first official, Gobbler's Knob, 2 Feb 1887; six more weeks)

questions.q: In 1934, observers on Mount Washington measured a 231 mph wind gust. Which state is it in?
questions.fact: It stood as the world record for a surface wind gust until a 1996 cyclone in Australia beat it.
questions.src: Verified: mprnews.org 2010/01/27 'New world wind record verified' (231 mph 1934 stood 62 years; 253 mph Barrow Island, Cyclone Olivia, 10 Apr 1996)

questions.q: On the Beaufort wind scale, which runs from 0 to 12, what is Force 12?
questions.fact: The scale is named for Francis Beaufort, a Royal Navy officer who devised it in 1805.
questions.src: Verified: rmets.org 'The Beaufort Wind Scale' (devised 1805 by Royal Navy officer Francis Beaufort; Force 10 storm, 11 violent storm, 12 hurricane)

blurb: Island nations, famous isles and castaways on page and screen

questions.q: Which island country is nicknamed the Emerald Isle?
questions.fact: Ireland is Europe's third-largest island, after Great Britain and Iceland.
questions.src: Verified: worldatlas.com largest islands of Europe (Great Britain, Iceland, Ireland)

questions.q: Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu and Shikoku are the four main islands of which country?
questions.fact: Honshu, the largest of the four, is home to Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto.

questions.q: Which Mediterranean island nation lies just south of Sicily?
questions.fact: Maltese and English are both official languages of Malta.

questions.q: Which island nation is named after a 16th-century king of Spain?
questions.fact: They were named in the 1540s for Spain's Prince Philip, later King Philip II; there are over 7,000 islands.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Names_of_the_Philippines (named 1543 by Villalobos's expedition for crown prince Philip, later Philip II)

questions.q: Not counting Australia, what is the largest island in the world?
questions.fact: Despite its name, about 80 percent of Greenland is covered by an ice sheet.
questions.src: Verified: livescience.com Greenland facts (ice sheet covers more than 80 percent)

questions.q: The Galapagos Islands, famous for giant tortoises, belong to which country?
questions.fact: Charles Darwin visited the islands aboard HMS Beagle in 1835.

questions.q: Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with which country?
questions.fact: Christopher Columbus landed there in 1492 and named it La Isla Espanola.

questions.q: The island of Zanzibar is part of which country?
questions.fact: Queen's Freddie Mercury was born there, and Tanzania's name blends Tanganyika and Zanzibar.

questions.q: The 2008 movie Mamma Mia! is set on a fictional island in which country?
questions.fact: Many of its location scenes were shot on the real Greek island of Skopelos.

questions.q: In the 2000 film Cast Away, Tom Hanks's character befriends a volleyball named what?
questions.fact: Its island scenes were shot on Monuriki, a small uninhabited island in Fiji.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monuriki (Cast Away filmed there; small uninhabited island, Mamanuca group, Fiji)

questions.q: On Gilligan's Island, what was the name of the boat that got shipwrecked?
questions.fact: Bob Denver played Gilligan, and Alan Hale Jr. played the Skipper.

questions.q: Robinson Crusoe Island, named for the castaway in Defoe's 1719 novel, belongs to which country?
questions.fact: Scottish sailor Alexander Selkirk, a likely model for Crusoe, lived alone there for over four years.

blurb: Snowflakes, ice and the animals that thrive in the cold

questions.q: How many sides does a typical snowflake have?
questions.fact: Snowflakes are six-sided because water molecules freeze into a hexagonal pattern.

questions.q: In the Inuit language Inuktitut, the word igloo means what?
questions.fact: Iglu can mean any kind of house, not just one built from blocks of snow.

questions.q: Buffalo, New York, is famous for lake-effect snow blowing off which Great Lake?
questions.fact: Lake-effect snow forms when frigid air crosses warmer lake water and picks up moisture.

questions.q: In 1885, Wilson Bentley became the first to photograph a single snowflake. In which state?
questions.fact: Bentley photographed more than 5,000 snowflakes and found no two exactly alike.
questions.src: Verified: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Bentley (first snowflake photo 15 Jan 1885; Jericho, VT farm; more than 5,000 images)

questions.q: Which continent holds most of the world's ice?
questions.fact: In places, Antarctica's ice sheet is more than 4 kilometers thick.

questions.q: Roughly how much of an iceberg's bulk is hidden below the waterline?
questions.fact: Icebergs are frozen fresh water that broke off glaciers or ice shelves.

questions.q: Ground that stays frozen for at least two years in a row is called what?
questions.fact: Permafrost lies beneath large parts of Alaska, northern Canada and Siberia.

questions.q: At what temperature do the Fahrenheit and Celsius scales show the same number?
questions.fact: That makes minus 40 the one temperature you never need to convert.

questions.q: What color is a polar bear's skin underneath its fur?
questions.fact: Polar bear fur is not truly white; each hair is see-through and scatters light, so it looks white.

questions.q: In the 2006 animated film Happy Feet, Mumble is which kind of penguin?
questions.fact: Emperors are the largest living penguins, and they breed through the bitter Antarctic winter.
questions.src: Verified: antarctica.gov.au emperor penguin page (largest of 18 species; breed during Antarctic winter)

questions.q: Which Arctic animal's coat turns from brown or gray in summer to white in winter?
questions.fact: Even the Arctic fox's paw pads are covered in fur, which helps it walk on snow and ice.

questions.q: Qiviut, one of the warmest natural wools, comes from which Arctic animal?
questions.fact: When threatened, musk oxen form a circle facing outward, with their young in the middle.
